story_review.one_viewing_summary: Water floods a San Antonio yard before a phone alert sounds. Researchers at UT San Antonio built a self-powered prototype station with four optical water sensors and weather instruments. A compact on-device TinyML chip assesses flood risk without connecting to a central server, then broadcasts long-range radio signals to a hub where a larger model maps flood paths. The reporting clearly establishes that the high accuracy figure is an early post-training validation metric, no field result is reported, no town is yet installed, and deployment remains an ongoing goal.
story_review.opening_to_ending: The film moves seamlessly from the human stakes of an unheralded flash flood to the technical engineering of a standalone prototype sensor node, detailing its local inference and telemetry, before candidly contextualizing the technology within its current un-deployed prototype limits.
story_review.weakest_transition: Cut from s6 to s7 at 38.16s, transitioning from the hub's second larger model map to the on-station chip validation card, which requires the voiceover to cleanly prevent confusion between the two AI models.

narration_picture_observations.observed: Brown water floods the yard past the curb and approaches rain boots on the step as the ankle-deep water clause is delivered.
Camera frames the smartphone lying on the rail, which vibrates and displays a late flash flood emergency notification banner.
The full prototype flood station is revealed on its pole at the waterlogged curb with a 'Prototype flood station' banner.
Sunlight strikes the solar panel, the green battery cells fill successively, and a dashed line stops short of a distant cell tower with a 'No cell tower needed' tag.
Camera examines four optical sensors mounted at staggered heights as water rises over them and weather instrument icons illuminate.
Close view inside the station housing shows white data pulses traveling along circuit traces from the sensors into the TinyML chip.
The TinyML chip triggers an amber flood risk lamp, 'Judged on the station' pins, and a distant dashed central server remains dark with no line connecting to it.
Amber radio waves pulse from the station whip antenna and expand down a residential street past a 'More than a half-mile' tag.
Radio wave pulses travel across open prairie terrain and terminate at a small hub building whose rooftop mast illuminates under an 'Up to five miles' marker.
At the hub desk, station points populate the screen and expanding amber flood zones highlight higher-risk corridors for emergency responders.
A card titled 'Validation accuracy' appears and an orange meter bar advances across the card to display the early validation record.
The validation figure 98.82% holds prominently on screen, accented by an 'Initial assessments after training' sub-tag.
The validation card slides to make room for an adjacent blank 'Field result' card, which is stamped with 'None reported'.
A town street grid map on a fence is scanned by a dashed search circle that finds no installed location, pinning a 'No installation named' banner.
A dashed goal pin hovers unlanded over the map while a dashed uninstalled ghost station draws itself at the roadside curb.

Require revision when it fails; a weakest\ninterval or a personal preference alone does not require another attempt.\n\n## What you are looking for\n\n**Genuine divergence, not a relabel.** Two scenes that both say \"wide establishing shot\" with\ndifferent nouns are one scene twice. Composition, camera move, scale and subject must actually\ndiffer.\n\n**Film-level construction.** Count `visual_family` and `payload_mode`, not just scene signatures.\nTwo families carrying most of the runtime or a sequence of figures delivered as text panels is a\nstructural ceiling. Props cannot repair it later.\n\n**The early payoff is a picture.** Read its deadline from `config/documentary.json`.\nScene one names a real strategy and visible payoff. An establishing shot, title, or promise\nthat something will become interesting later is not a hook.\n\n**Picture-led.** Follow the action with the narration and labels covered. If the story\nonly works with narration, it is a podcast with pictures and it fails here.\n\n**Input is not processing proof.** If narration describes scanning, analyzing, selecting or another transformation, a captured input image alone does not prove that action. The current phone film must show the transformation and a completed visible consequence in the same objects. Captions may explain scope; they cannot supply a missing action. A retained still can be valid evidence, but an unchanged inset is not an analysis beat. Compare the native rejection interval with the new phone pixels before approving the same mechanism again.\n\n**Judge the dominant picture, not peripheral motion.** A small moving sliver behind a large static inset does not repair the inset's pacing. Inspect the actual native hero at phone size and native crop scale: recognizable silhouettes at 270 pixels can conceal unfinished surfaces, faceted props and missing contact shadows. Compare all unresolved native defects together before the next render; do not approve a label, outline or tiny prop change as a complete repair. If the same dominant layout has failed twice, require a changed composition or action mechanism before another native attempt.\n\n**Sentence-to-pixel proof.** Ignore `on_screen`, `what_moves` and `hero` on the first pass. For\neach VO line, inspect `visual_proof.must_show`, resolve every `item_id` into `planes[].items`, and\nask whether those actual components and props make the sentence literal. A generic pickup under a\nreadout is not a model joining records. If the binding is technically present but visually tiny\nor dominated by unrelated context, revise it.\n\n**Docket flow.** The scene roles should cause one another: movement, consequence, honest limit,\nthen agency. A list of facts can be accurate and still have no story. The close should answer\n\"what happens next\" rather than merely restate the hook.\n\n**Attention earns each interval.** Read `config/documentary.json` and the craft guide. Resolve\n`attention_beats` through the scene event ids, including the gap to the ending. The hook must\nactually pay off within the policy window. A line of text, a camera drift or an animated dash\ncannot rescue a subject that does nothing. The faster direction asks for action, consequence,\nevidence or human response while preserving time to understand each idea.\n\n**Motivated framing.** The camera can hold while a subject acts or evidence is read. Move it to\nreveal a relationship, follow an action or change the viewer's understanding. Do not add orbiting\nor zooming merely to advertise the engine. A continuous action may span multiple scene records.\n\n**Three images before a finished film.** Identify the opening payoff, central mechanism and\nclosing consequence. Ask which image will be remembered and what question it resolves. If these\nare three cards with labels, reboard before spending a render. Check the actual source of every\nreconstruction and whether its visual certainty exceeds the reporting.\n\n**Visual access before visual promises.** For each of those three images, name the public\nreference or source fact that permits its depiction. If the pivotal action occurs inside a\nprivate interface, lab or workplace that no source shows, do not approve a sequence of invented\nscreens and pointing gestures as observed workflow. Require an explicitly illustrated mechanism\nwhose state visibly changes, or send the director back to a more filmable source-backed angle.\nAn event list with verbs is insufficient when the same generic panel remains the dominant image.\n\n**Region correctness.** The scene's region comes from the story's county. A supported prop or clear\nsilhouette alone cannot clear those defects. Existing source, rights, action, native, audio, captions,\ncumulative resources, finite artistic recovery and shipment requirements continue.\n\n## Director\n\nBefore coding, choose the visual approach from actual source access. Think through four\nlenses in the existing director assignment: the comedian finds an observable mismatch;\nthe dramatist finds pressure and a changed state; the explainer finds the causal relation;\nthe enthusiast finds a specific surprising detail. Do not invent a joke, conflict or\noutcome. Choose exactly two complete treatments within the current comparison allowance.\n\nWrite `art_direction` in each board using `config/art_direction.json`. Explain seven palette\nroles, contrasting shapes, the recognizable hero silhouette and its finish, motivated\nlight, focal hierarchy, action timing, and one signature shot tied to an actual event.\nName the current asset and actual subject ids. Use the source image itself when it is the\nhero. Give a dimensional scene a `shots[scene_id]` camera position, target, lens and reason;\nan event-bound `to` pose is optional. For the illustrated carton route, use `flat_shots`\nwith native-coordinate offsets, scale and a reason. Numeric shot choices must be executed\nby the routed scene, not left as board prose. A custom renderer must consume the same\nprofile or explain its retained source lighting and implement its relevant choices.\n\nThe focal object stays sharp. Depth blur must arise from actual separation and preserve\ncontact detail. Never add blur, floating shapes, lens flares, camera kicks or orbiting as\nautomatic cinematic decoration. Hold the camera while an object performs. Move it to reveal\na relation or follow a finite action. Give a completed result a comprehension hold.\n\n## Scene builder and render owner\n\nUse `prompts/roles/scene-builder.md` in the existing code assignment. Build the finished\nhero first, then light and stage it before extending the scene. Recognizable geometry,\nedges, seams, hardware, texture and grounded shadows beat a field of placeholder primitives.\nAuthored 2.5D, useful footage and a readable source image can outperform complicated 3D.\nDo not restrict the daily story to the demonstration subject or copy reference b-roll.\n\nThe shared `ArtDirectionProvider` carries current choices in both entry points. Three.js\n`CinematicStage`/`Studio` execute the light recipe and exposure. `directedShot` executes\nauthored event-bound cameras. The illustrated carton component executes its flat framing,\nfinished surfaces, occlusion and contact assemblies. Source footage retains original speed\nand practical lighting. Existing boards without this profile retain their original defaults.\n\nEvery new event specifies a motion curve within its existing measured window: `travel`\naccelerates and brakes; `contact` approaches and settles; `linear` serves constant-speed\nmovement; `smoothstep` is available for a justified gentle transition. `anticipation` and\n`settle` reserve fractions inside that window, never new runtime or voice stretching.\n`landing` has a small overshoot and needs a free-prop reason; never use it for a constrained\ncontact, a foot planted on ground, or a source-implied machine limit. Check music and foley\nagainst the executed contact, not the old curve. No incidental sway substitutes for action.\n\nJudge motion at the delivered 30 fps. A regular frame clock does not excuse abrupt starts,\nfast screen-space travel or repeated stop-and-go strokes. Directed `travel` and `contact`\ncurves start and finish with zero velocity and acceleration. Give a heavy load enough of\nthe existing scene window to accelerate and brake. Holds consume that window; do not squeeze\nthe entire stroke into the remaining few frames. Inspect velocity at event joins as well\nas the start and end. Keep a clear contact view and a stable camera when tracking amplifies\nthe load's movement. Do not conceal stepping with blur, frame interpolation or faster audio.\nAn event-bound moving camera uses `travel` or `contact`; the input check refuses constant-speed\nstarts and landing overshoot on a camera. Hold it when the object needs a different curve.\n\nWhen two named events describe successive stages of one uninterrupted movement, author\nadjacent windows with no interior anticipation or settle, then explicitly use\n`joinedActionWindow`. The helper rejects gaps, scene boundaries and erased rests. The\nillustrated carton route consumes `continuous_withdrawal_event_ids` only in its withdrawal\nscene. Retiming a movement keeps the source relation, scene runtime and measured captions.\n\n## Existing independent critic and three scorers\n\nWatch the actual muted sequence first. Name the object, action, changed state and answered\nquestion before reading the profile. Then test whether its choices are visible: compare\nsilhouette, contact, surface finish, hierarchy, framing, rhythm and hold at phone size and\nnative crop scale. A good explanation in the profile cannot clear an\noccluded grip, generic slab, unrecognizable subject or absent transformation.\n\nWatch uninterrupted playback at normal speed. Check for velocity jumps, stop-and-go camera\ntracking, repeated frames during movement and excessively large per-frame displacement.\nSeparate deliberate shot cuts and completed holds from a continuous stroke that stutters.\nRecord the exact interval and affected object or camera. Smooth motion is a visible property,\nnot a consequence of a passing score or a high frame rate.\n\nRead `knowledge/craft/cinematic_reference_bank.json`. Its frozen passages teach specific\ndecisions; their old scores use different rubrics and are not comparable ratings. They are\nreferences, never production assets or current approval. Compare two current complete cuts,\ndescribe a preference with exact times, then record mandatory defects under the existing\ncriteria. A different palette preference alone does not create another correction. Retain\nall original rejections. At the configured artistic boundary, finish the strongest credible\ncut; source, comprehension and technical failures still take the mandatory recovery route.\n\n## Learn from shipped and failed footage\n\n`scripts/cinematic_learning.py` records the next five editions from the policy's effective\ndate, including unfinished editions, first-panel success, scores, all actual resource usage,\nprovider tokens, elapsed time, correction counts and artistic deferrals. At most once per seven days, give the existing builder a fresh compact packet:\nup to five recurring findings, exact rejected evidence and one proposed shared capability.\nReproduce the failed interval; add a useful regression; prove the correction inside the next\nedition's already reserved two-treatment comparison. Mark the actual advance or honest skip\nin the packet. The fresh charged review must inspect\nthe complete retained current direction and current source evidence before production resumes.\n\n```sh\npython scripts/narration_recovery.py --state out/dispatch/run_state.json --receipt <actual-receipt> --report <full-original-rejection> --output <new-capacity-plan>\npython scripts/run_controller.py production-budget --review-route host --repair-plan <new-capacity-plan>\npython scripts/run_controller.py completion-capacity --repair-plan <new-capacity-plan>\npython scripts/run_controller.py production-budget --review-route host --repair-plan <new-capacity-plan>\npython scripts/narration_recovery.py --state out/dispatch/run_state.json --settle-unreserved <new-capacity-plan>\n```\n\nUse the environment wrapper and explicit internal cd. Both fresh phone reviews and all shipment gates remain required.\n","knowledge/craft/BOUNDED_CREATIVE_RELEASE.md":"# Finite creative repair and autonomous shipment\n\nOwner instruction from October 3rd, 2026. This policy replaces the dimensional opening\nand runtime quota. All source, quality, independent review, native output, audio, caption,\nbudget and shipment requirements remain. Missing or contradictory explanation stays a comprehension/source defect under the\ncurrent contract; decorative motion can't turn it into a deferrable style issue.\n\nRetain the same two-treatment batch, frozen budget, native hero, independent reviews and\nbounded-release route. The [October 2nd pavement diagnosis](visual-storytelling/october-2-pavement-case.md)\nis a sampled-frame case study, not a replacement verdict or permission to alter the shipped film.\n\n## Treatment recovery from September 30, 2026\n\nSeptember 29 is a rejected creative reference. Its source screenshots, repeated fading boxes\nand growing underlines never became an engaging film. Use the source to discover a physical\ntask, obstacle and consequence. Preserve that action in the script and pictures. Authentic\nimagery earns a shot when it reveals something; a relevant document is not automatically\nthe film's subject. Original source-grounded illustration and demonstrated action remain\nfirst-class choices. Reuse proven components, never prior-edition photographic assets.\n\nStart with one credible demonstrated treatment and one genuinely different visual treatment.\nCompare their action, composition and viewer payoff in the existing batch. If both fail,\nuse one consolidated mechanism-changing simplification before narration; do not keep tuning\nthe same weak presentation. Preserve the strongest accepted complete preview as the fallback.\nNo extra research pass, reviewer role, third speculative concept or bespoke rig is authorized.\n\nThe existing critic must judge the whole film against the prior successful visual standard.\nNamed cities, correct labels and readable source text do not establish strong picture or place.\nA code pass for geometry and provenance does not establish an engaging treatment. Inspect\nthe opening, middle and ending as actual action before refining layout. Give each cut its own\nvisible reason; repeated prose cannot direct ten different shots.\n\n## Choose the story from its tangible stakes\n\nBefore narration, selected.visual_stakes records affected_person, physical_subject,\nvisible_change, consequence, opening_question, answer, asset_fit and source_urls. Name the\nspecific worker, resident or group and what changes for them. Tie the opening question to the\nanswer that the available evidence can support. Prefer the most informative authentic image. Apply the no-repeat policy in\nDAILY_PRODUCTION.md. Use source-still or source-excerpt candidate rows with asset_url and the\nsame inspection/rights evidence as source-footage. Diagram rows need a sourced relationship\nand disclosure Illustration. Each scene still needs a\nfilmable subject, action, consequence and source_basis. Geometry is useful when depth or contact\nexplains something. Footage is useful when the action is actually visible. A still can establish\na real place; an excerpt can expose the decisive words; a diagram can explain a sourced relation.\nDo not force a character into a source image or draw a fake room to meet a quota.\n\nThe editorial-v1 route accepts each scene's picture with id, medium, event_id, disclosure and\nsubject (the inspected subject, checked by the critic). Use it to reveal a real detail, never imply a machine detected it.\nSource-excerpt renders the actual inspected page image, preserving its words. Diagram nodes\ncarry short label and claim_id; two to four nodes appear on the event clock. The source and\nnumeral gates cover those printed labels. No long paragraphs or substitute dashboards.\nDimensional scenes omit picture and call the existing demonstrated action route; bespoke\nsource-backed mechanisms retain their admission and native-hero requirements.\n\nEvery current scene receives full-resolution normal/subject-removed sample pairs. Otherwise the principal picture must visibly develop on its event clock.\nThe hero remains a finished native passage with sound, even when it uses no 3D.\n\n## Compare two openings once\n\nPrepare opening-a.json and opening-b.json beside storyboard.json. It reserves one preflight batch, renders exactly two\nquarter-scale full animatics with one browser/bundle, and saves openings/comparison.json.\nBoth completed films receive exact-board, film, renderer and inspector-bound structural reports\nbefore phone review. Its --retain-failed-inspection flag retains\ndiagnostics for policy-authorized finishing only; it does not change a failed report or approve\nphone review. The unused option stays as evidence. Neither option authorizes a narration take until\nthe chosen cut passes the current phone gate. After any\nstructural change, review the whole sequence. Each cue has id,\nevent_id, role (environment, contact, sonification or quiet), duration_s, intent and provenance.\nUse truthful recorded ambience or an explicitly designed effect. The quiet cue reduces the music and\neffects bus on its actual visual event; it never mutes, stretches or splices the narration.\n\nEach non-quiet cue has one sfx_events entry with matching id/event_id, wav, source and gain.\nThe mixer anchors it to the current board event, trims to its declared duration at original\nspeed, adds short edge fades and refuses undersized or nonfinite audio. It records every cue,\nsource WAV hash and the exact sound/timing digest in mix.json. Retime the sfx event file with the\nboard and remix after a changed clock. Old mix evidence fails the release check.\n\nThe existing voice director reads this sound arc and the selected opening. It binds\nsound_direction_sha256 to the sound object and gives each line specific intent, relative energy\nand an exact spoken emphasis phrase. One continuous take\nand its existing audible soundcheck remain the default; field completion cannot approve a flat\nor synthetic read. The sound lens judges actual delivery, masking, sync and contrast in the MP4.\n\nAll three final audiovisual lenses and scoring agents remain. The legacy response field\ndimensional_action describes the principal picture in any medium. A judge may reject a weak\nimage, inert diagram, generic read or unearned cut with timestamped evidence; a medium preference\nalone is not a defect. Passing quality moves directly to release and verified shipment.\n","knowledge/craft/MODERN_FILM.md":{"$text":["# Direct the film before describing its look\n\nOwner instruction, October 7th, 2026. Palette, camera poses and declared events did not create a visual argument.\nThe bounded release contract could also defer pacing, motion, surface finish and ending artistry.\nNeither a score nor a completed worksheet overrules that observed failure.\n\nThis upgrade therefore changes the executable route and review eligibility. Capacity recovery funds mandatory repair on the\ncurrent route; it never restores the retired route or edits a rejected finding.\n\n## Lessons verified in AlaskaAIWeekly\n\nStudy pinned source and complete published films, rather than an isolated hero still. Keep camera movement motivated and finite; do not copy every decorative effect from a stronger reference.\"\n  }\n}\n","knowledge/craft/visual-storytelling/README.md":"# Visual storytelling for Dispatch\n\nResearch and direction revision: October 2nd, 2026.\n\nThe picture, narration and captions must describe the same unfolding story. The picture supplies a recognizable subject, relationship, action or consequence. Narration explains its significance and limits. Captions give access to the spoken account. A moving object is useful only when the viewer understands what it represents and what its change means.\n\nThese dossiers combine researched craft with proposed Dispatch practice. Source observations are identified and linked. The shot methods, selection procedure and worked example are our production recommendations, not claims that research guarantees audience engagement.\n\n## Choose the story's visual approach\n\nRead this index and the chosen dossier in full before boarding. Select by the available evidence and the explanation the viewer needs. Keep one primary approach; supporting footage or documents should connect to that approach through a clear subject or question.\n\n| Approach | Choose when | What it must show | Reject when |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| [Observed documentary](observed-documentary.md) | Authenticated footage shows the actual people, place, equipment or workflow | A real action and its observed result | Similar-looking stock replaces the story's actual identity |\n| [Explanatory animation](explanatory-animation.md) | The central process or comparison is hard to see directly | Recognizable input, meaningful transformation and readable output | Abstract objects require a private legend to decode |\n| [Evidence-led imagery](evidence-led-imagery.md) | Relevant photographs or documents carry the reporting | What the evidence establishes and how it changes the answer | A sequence of screenshots substitutes for the entire mechanism |\n| [Cinematic scene](cinematic-scene.md) | A source-backed physical task, obstacle and consequence can sustain a scene | Spatially coherent action, a turn and a consequential ending | Lighting, orbiting props or music replace story development |\n\nUse this selection order:\n\n1. State the viewer's question, sourced action, affected person or group and honest ending.\n2. Inventory inspected, usable assets and demonstrated components. Record what each can and can't show.\n3. Choose the approach that makes the central relationship easiest to understand. Explain the rejected alternative in one sentence.\n4. Complete the [sentence-to-shot worksheet](sentence-to-shot.md). Resolve missing pictures before locking narration.\n5. Compare exactly two genuinely different complete treatments in the existing shared preview batch. Read the selected dossier for each treatment. Preserve the current contracts, frozen budget and existing independent roles.\n6. Have the existing critic inspect the actual rendered sequence before reading the director's explanation. A filled worksheet does not prove comprehension.\n\nDo not impose a weekday rotation. Track the selected approach in the existing creative-direction rationale so the director can see recent repetition. When two approaches fit equally well, variety can break the tie. Never choose variety at the expense of truth or comprehension.\n\n## Choose a format and think through its sequence\n\nFor newly planned editions from October 3rd, read the [viewer planning method](viewer-plan.md) in full. Distinguish the format from the medium: a news report can use observed footage, illustration or documents; an educational explainer can return from a diagram to physical evidence; a cinematic scene still needs a truthful task and consequence.\n\nFor a news report read [the reporting dossier](news-reporting.md) and choose its human-led, mechanism-led or evidence-led structure from the actual story. Record why the order works, the likely false inference and the carried subject across each cut in the existing creative-direction and transition fields. The [national-news study](broadcast-cadence-study.md) identifies the observed examples and access limits. It does not prescribe a single bracketed rundown.\n\nThe director and workers use these short decision reasons to choose and challenge the treatment. A copied structure, named style or completed worksheet supplies no quality verdict. The packet tools bind the current method and relevant approach text; remote recovery supplies the actual text because a provider can't open local links.\n\n## Give the three channels distinct jobs\n\n**See:** Show the thing being discussed at the moment it is discussed. Preserve its identity across the cut. Make any comparison legible before asking the viewer to infer a result.\n\n**Hear:** Name the relationship, cause or uncertainty that the picture can't establish alone. Time emphasis and event sound to the actual reveal. A music swell can't supply an unreported outcome.\n\n**Read:** Retain complete measured captions. Use brief object labels only where they identify a picture or distinction. Avoid simultaneous paragraph copy competing with both the action and captions. Lay out the decisive result above the real caption band and hold it long enough to understand.\n\nMayer's research summary supports removing distracting content, placing related words near pictures and presenting corresponding animation and narration together. It also reports redundancy effects in multimedia learning. These are learning findings, not a forecast of short-video retention; they do not justify removing accessible captions. Our application is to reduce competing editorial text while maintaining captions. [Cambridge multimedia-learning chapter](https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/abs/cambridge-handbook-of-multimedia-learning/principles-for-reducing-extraneous-processing-in-multimedia-learning-coherence-signaling-redundancy-spatial-contiguity-and-temporal-contiguity-principles/C98AB3A6CE760DD63C048936EA0B3B44), [W3C caption guidance](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/captions-prerecorded).\n\n## Review what the viewer receives\n\nUse the existing review assignments and fixed rubric. Add these observations to their existing consolidated notes, not a new scorecard or paid role.\n\n- **Recognition:** Before reading the board, what does the principal object look like? Can the critic name it without guessing?\n- **Alignment:** At each narrated clause, does the picture show the named subject and relationship? Record exact film times for contradictions or absent concepts.\n- **Development:** What changed, and how does that change lead to the next shot? Distinguish subject transformation from decorative motion.\n- **Continuity:** Is the same person, site, sample or document being followed? Is a different example disclosed?\n- **Combined comprehension:** After one viewing with audio and captions, what happened, who can act and what remains unproven?\n- **Picture contribution:** With narration muted and captions covered, which parts of the central process can the viewer actually see? Dates and attribution may rely on text; the principal action can't.\n- **Ending:** Does the final picture answer the opening question without inventing implementation, savings, approval or repair?\n\nAn unrecognizable object, absent principal action or contradictory picture is a comprehension/source defect under the current contract. Do not classify it as merely style because pixels move. Surface polish and optional camera preferences remain artistic issues. Retain all real rejected verdicts and use the existing repair and bounded-release policies.\n\n## Apply this without expanding production\n\nUse the current budget precheck for the complete review and render path before spending. Research access does not grant reuse rights to any publisher's images, footage or soundtrack.\n","knowledge/craft/visual-storytelling/explanatory-animation.md":"# Explanatory animation\n\nRead the [shared visual-storytelling direction](README.md) first.\n\n## What this approach does\n\nIt makes a hidden process or comparison understandable: two inputs contributing different information, a record moving through a decision, or a physical condition producing a visible measurement. Original diagrams and illustration are often the clearest first choice.\n\nChoose this approach when the source establishes the relationship but useful observational footage is missing or can't reveal it. The explanation must preserve the source's uncertainty and distinguish a conceptual example from an actual system output.\n\n## Research findings and limits\n\nAdobe describes the storyboard as a bridge from script to picture, with panels recording action, dialogue and camera requirements, followed by an animatic to examine the sequence. Its guide includes side-by-side storyboard references for Luca and Up. Those links are study examples; we have not claimed a shot analysis of those films here. [Adobe storyboarding guide](https://www.adobe.com/uk/creativecloud/animation/discover/animation-storyboarding.html).\n\nThe [shared direction's learning research](README.md) motivates coordinated explanation and reduced distraction. It does not prove that more animation improves understanding. The following construction method is a Dispatch recommendation responding to the actual pavement-film defect.\n\n## Build the explanation\n\nWrite the relationship in plain words before choosing objects. For pavement research: surface imagery and depth information reveal different properties of the same road condition. This is a comparison of information, not a story about two blocks traveling on a conveyor.\n\n1. **Show the input.** Give it a recognizable form. A photograph should look like a surface image. A document should have a credible readable structure. A road should look like a road.\n2. **Introduce one distinction.** Use short labels next to the relevant views. Keep the same sample identity and orientation.\n3. **Show the operation.** Reveal a cross-section, align corresponding views or trace a source-supported relationship. The operation must change what the viewer can understand.\n4. **Show the result.** Keep the resulting distinction readable. Do not hide it beneath captions, replace it with a flash or move immediately to another object.\n5. **Show the decision or limit.** Connect the output to the source-backed choice. Leave unproven implementation visibly unresolved.\n\nUse arrows to connect a known relationship, not to pretend that an unavailable algorithm has been observed. A bright scan bar is not analysis proof by itself. Do not invent segmentation accuracy, measured depths, confidence percentages or a vendor interface.\n\nChoose 2D, 2.5D or 3D based on the relationship. A flat comparison often explains two images best. A cutaway can reveal depth. A three-dimensional scene earns its cost when spatial interaction is the explanation; a beveled box representing an unfamiliar object often adds interpretation work.\n\n## Stage and time the picture\n\nMake the principal forms identifiable before their transformation. Maintain consistent labels, positions and shape cues. Use color as support, with readable shape or text distinctions as well. Introduce a new concept only after the current relationship is clear.\n\nPlan the reveal around the relevant spoken clause, then use measured narration timing for the final event windows. Quiet or restrained sound can mark a visible comparison; a synthetic beep can't imply actual hardware recording. Preserve the existing sound and caption contracts.\n\nA changed state can be information made visible. It need not be a moving human or a mechanical handoff. The current minimum picture-action contract still applies: a full-film static diagram with decorative fades is a rejected treatment.\n\n## Worked pattern\n\n| Spoken idea | Useful picture | Inadequate substitute |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| A photo shows the surface | A recognizable top-down pavement image | An unlabeled gray slab |\n| Depth adds another kind of information | Corresponding depth view or disclosed conceptual cutaway | A floating yellow rail |\n| Damage differs from a stain | Stable side-by-side comparison with the difference revealed | Two different props swapping places |\n| The result supports a report | A recognizable illustrative report linked to the example | Blank sheets flying into trays |\n| Detection is not repair | Return to the unchanged physical damage | A celebratory completion animation |\n\nThis pattern is conceptual guidance, not a verified reconstruction of Texas State's UI or numerical output. See the [pavement case](october-2-pavement-case.md) for source limits.\n\n## Before voice and final review\n\nHave the existing critic first name the pictured objects and explain the relationship without the director's legend. Then compare exact spoken clauses to rendered moments. If the critic needs the board to identify the principal input or result, consolidate that as a comprehension defect before narration.\n\nUse proven components and the existing shared preview comparison. Test the hardest current transformation in the native hero. Preserve the strongest accepted complete treatment as the completion fallback. Additional labels, texture or camera movement can't repair a missing explanation.\n","knowledge/craft/visual-storytelling/news-reporting.md":"# Direct a coherent news report\n\nThe [cadence study](broadcast-cadence-study.md) records the evidence behind this dossier. The structures below are Dispatch production choices, not a universal network script. Apply them to newly planned editions from October 3rd, 2026; preserve shipped editions and their real reviews.\n\nA report has an editorial spine: a specific situation, a question, evidence that changes the answer, an explanation, an honest consequence and a close. Decide which of those jobs the next shot performs. A source-related image that supplies no new understanding is a weak insert, even if its colors and motion look expensive.\n\n## Choose the order from the story\n\n| Reporting structure | Choose it when | Sequence of reporting jobs | Ending test |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| Human-led report | The evidence identifies a real person's task, obstacle or changed options | Show the task or consequence \u2192 establish the dated change \u2192 broaden with evidence \u2192 explain the cause and limits \u2192 return to the same person or task | Has the viewer learned what changes for that person, without an invented reaction or outcome? |\n| Mechanism-led report | The central news is a process, measurement or decision that viewers can't readily see | Show a recognizable input and question \u2192 orient the source and setting \u2192 reveal the transformation \u2192 show the result \u2192 connect it to a human decision and its limits | Can the viewer explain the input, transformation and result, and distinguish an illustration from observed operation? |\n| Evidence-led report | A filing, policy, measurement or public record changes the reported answer | Establish the dated decision or disputed claim \u2192 expose the decisive source detail \u2192 explain its effect with a concrete relationship \u2192 show affected options or activity \u2192 state the unresolved point and next decision | Does the ending answer what the record establishes, who can act next and what it does not establish? |\n\nChoose one structure. Compress or reorder it when the evidence and viewer's question justify that choice. Establish the essential source limitation when the affected claim appears; a later caveat can't undo a misleading picture. Keep the current early-picture payoff and event timing requirements. These sequences introduce no extra scenes, prescribed shot seconds or runtime quota.\n\nThe CBS transcript in the study provides a specific-to-broad-to-specific example. The CNN transcript shows a different package organization, and the MSNBC example is a question-led interview. They are different forms with different access to people and evidence. A short Dispatch should not imitate a lengthy panel simply because it resembles national television.\n\n## Assign each ingredient a reporting job\n\n**Opening:** Give the viewer something identifiable to understand immediately: a task interrupted, an input changing, a decision confronting evidence, or a completed consequence that creates a question. State the actual question soon enough to guide the picture. A dramatic claim must stay within the fetched evidence. Do not borrow an unrelated victim, emergency or reaction to manufacture stakes.\n\n**Orientation:** Establish who, where and what changed using the minimum needed narration and labels. This is the short-video equivalent of the paragraph that explains the focus of an article. The viewer should know why the next piece of evidence belongs in this story.\n\n**Reporter or presenter:** Use an actual reusable field passage when it demonstrates, verifies or bridges the explanation. A fabricated journalist, microphone prop or studio cut adds no verification. Dispatch's narrator can orient the viewer without appearing as a reporter. A person on screen must have a source-backed role and perform an understandable action.\n\n**Evidence:** Show the exact place, equipment, task, relevant photograph or decisive source words. Identify what the evidence establishes. A quotation is evidence of what its speaker said; it is not proof that their conclusion is true. Show a contrary finding or uncertainty when the story requires it. Use the existing source and rights lanes for every asset.\n\n**Explanation:** Introduce coded visuals when they reveal a relationship that the authentic image can't show. Keep the same physical subject or explicitly identify the new example. The diagram should answer the question created by the preceding shot. Return to the source image or human decision after the explanation when that return completes the thought.\n\n**Consequence and close:** Show how the action changes a state, choice, risk or next step. Answer the opening question through the completed visible action. Distinguish a demonstrated consequence, an expected effect and an unknown eventual outcome. Do not repeat the introduction merely to make the film seem circular. A return earns its place when the viewer now understands the original subject differently.\n\n## Move between authentic pictures and coded explanation\n\nMake each handoff explicit in the existing edit notes. Carry a stable identifying detail: the same road patch, sample, site, device, document passage or clearly disclosed example. Preserve orientation, useful scale and the relationship under explanation. An outline or highlight identifies a region; it does not prove that a machine detected, measured or classified it.\n\nFor example, an authenticated image can establish the input. An explicitly illustrated transformation can explain the source-supported relationship. A return to the actual task can show who uses the result. Cutting from an unrelated office image to anonymous blocks and then to a different city breaks that connection, even if every image is broadly about AI.\n\nOriginal illustration is a valid principal medium. Useful footage is also valid. An irrelevant insert should be omitted within the existing bounded search. Do not commission an unproven rig or prolong the stock hunt to imitate a particular outlet. Use the current source-backed action admission when a genuinely necessary mechanism needs implementation.\n\n## Direct the cadence across picture, voice and reading\n\nGive each beat one new idea the viewer needs for the next beat. Complete its decisive event before cutting. Preserve enough time to recognize the subject, follow the change and read the result. Trim repeated setup before requesting faster narration. Pace varies with information and action; a cut on a fixed timer is not an editorial reason.\n\nVoice should orient, reveal, explain, qualify or resolve. Tell the VO director which job a line performs and where the visual answer lands. Keep the approved continuous script and measured alignment. Use contrast in intent and emphasis rather than perpetual urgency. Do not turn a hypothesis into certainty through a triumphant delivery or sound cue.\n\nNatural sound, verified interview audio and motivated effects can connect thoughts when their provenance and actual event timing support that use. A sound bridge can carry the same action over a cut. Sound can't imply recorded access to a site we did not visit. Preserve intelligibility and all existing audio checks.\n\nRetain complete captions. Keep extra labels short and attached to the object they identify. Do not present a second paragraph, a busy diagram and a new location at the same time as a dense spoken sentence. Seeing, hearing and reading should reinforce the same unfolding account.\n\n## Review the actual report\n\nThe existing critic and scorers reconstruct the story from the current film before consulting the director's rationale. They identify what the opening asks, what new information arrives in the middle, how subject identity survives each handoff, and what the ending answers. Then they compare that understanding with the approved words and fetched evidence.\n\nUse exact intervals and the existing observation fields. A missing principal action, unrecognizable subject, false visual implication or failed explanation remains a source/comprehension failure under the current contract. Optional presenter preferences, shot polish and an alternative ordering alone do not create a new mandatory test. Keep the fixed rubric and retain every actual rejection.\n","knowledge/craft/visual-storytelling/viewer-plan.md":"# Make the editorial choice before the picture\n\nApply this method to newly planned editions from October 3rd, 2026. It guides decisions under the current contracts and does not certify quality. Use the existing creative_direction and story_contract fields; keep the decision rationale compact and inspectable.\n\n1. **Focus.** In viewer_question and visible_answer, state what changes, for whom, through which sourced action. Name the expected viewer takeaway and the strongest honest limit. Distinguish the narrative answer from an unknown eventual outcome.\n2. **Choose.** Begin medium_choice with the named format and approach: News report, Educational explainer or Cinematic scene; then Observed documentary, Explanatory animation, Evidence-led imagery or Cinematic scene. Explain why the available assets can carry the explanation and why a plausible alternative is weaker. Naming an approach is a routing aid, not an approval field.\n3. **Order.** Put each beat's reporting job in the existing scene advances and edit notes. For a report choose human-led, mechanism-led or evidence-led ordering. Explain why this evidence appears here and what question it creates or answers. Educational explanation builds a recognizable example through successive states. A cinematic scene follows a task, obstacle, consequential turn and completed action. Do not apply one rundown to all three.\n4. **Anticipate confusion.** Name the most likely false inference and the picture or immediate source limit that prevents it. In emotional_turn, connect the viewer's changing understanding to an evidenced stake. Do not invent a person's feelings or claim to know the audience's reaction.\n5. **Connect.** In enter_on, leave_on, cut_after_event_id and next_connection, name the visible event, new information and carried subject. Complete the event before the cut. A footage-to-diagram handoff keeps the same identified example or discloses a new one. Finish the sentence-to-shot worksheet inside these existing notes.\n6. **Direct and test.** Tie line intent, emphasis, motivated sound and captions to the actual reveal. Before spending, ask what remains understandable with narration muted and editorial labels covered, then test the combined account. Essential dates and attribution can use text; the principal action must read in the picture. Budget the entire remaining review/render path, including independent-provider recovery where required.\n\nThese are short decision reasons a colleague can inspect, not a request for a private stream of thought. Use concrete evidence and an alternative that could realistically be built. Do not fill every field with the same sentence, duplicate the research or commission a third treatment.\n\n## Each worker has a distinct decision\n\n- **Researcher:** Identify the most informative picture and the strongest limitation. catch local floods\n\nSeptember 8, 2026\n\n4 minutes\n\nAudrey Gray\n\nShare this story\n\nChen Pan\nWhen sudden rainstorms roll across Texas, flooding can erupt in a matter of minutes. From coastal bends facing storm surges to low-water crossings in San Antonio, flood risks often spike block by block long before regional alerts sound. That means some people could have ankle-deep water in their yard by the time a flash flood warning notification sounds on their phone.\nBut a better monitoring system could get the word out more swiftly \u2014 and also more accurately. Researchers at The University of Texas at San Antonio have developed a self-sustaining, artificial intelligence-powered flood warning system designed to spot dangerous water accumulation at the street level.\nLed by Chen Pan , PhD, assistant professor of electrical engineering in the Margie and Bill Klesse College of Engineering and Integrated Design, the team engineered a field-ready prototype that combines solar energy harvesting, multi-sensor environmental tracking, long-range wireless radios and on-device machine learning.\n\u201cIn many rural areas or coastal communities, power infrastructure can fail right when severe weather strikes,\u201d said Pan, who directs the RISE Lab at UT San Antonio. \u201cOur system is an off-grid solution. It generates its own power, evaluates flood risk locally right on the device and sends timely warnings without needing external electricity or expensive network lines.\u201d\nThe team includes Mimi Xie , assistant professor of computer science in the UT San Antonio College of AI, Cyber and Computing, as well as Texas A&M University-Corpus Christi collaborators Hua Zhang , professor of engineering, and Wenlu Wang , assistant professor of computer science.\nThe challenge of hyper-local flooding in Texas This project was funded in part by a Texas Coastal Management Program grant awarded by the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA).\nTexas holds a well-earned reputation for extreme flood events. While regional weather models and satellite imaging offer essential big-picture forecasts, they can miss hyper-local flash floods. A drainage channel behind a neighborhood, an isolated rural dip or a campus access road might submerge rapidly while surrounding areas remain dry.\nExisting commercial flood-monitoring stations also come with drawbacks, from prohibitively high costs to reliance on grid power or frequent battery replacements, which leaves them vulnerable during multi-day storms or power outages.\nPan\u2019s team set out to engineer an inexpensive, all-in-one alternative. The resulting prototype combines temperature, humidity, light and precipitation sensing, as well as four optical water-level sensors mounted at varying heights.\nBy analyzing multiple environmental factors simultaneously \u2014 an approach known as multi-modal sensing \u2014 the system achieves far greater reliability than traditional single-metric gauges.\nPutting artificial intelligence directly on tiny computer chips\nOne of the system\u2019s standout features is its exceptional computing power. Traditional Internet of Things (IoT) sensors simply collect raw data and transmit them to distant cloud servers for processing. If cell towers fail or internet connections drop during a storm, warning alerts stall.\nPan\u2019s system sidesteps this roadblock by using TinyML \u2014 a branch of computer science that compresses machine learning algorithms so they can run directly on small, low-power microcontrollers. This on-device AI evaluates current and recent sensor data to predict localized, imminent flood risk without relying on a central server.\nSo far, the AI has performed well, achieving 98.82% validation accuracy in initial assessments post-training.\nOff-grid power and long-range wireless communication\nTo keep operating through heavy storms and overcast days, the sensing node relies on a self-sustaining solar power system. An onboard power chip collects ambient light to charge a built-in battery and backup energy storage units, allowing the device to run indefinitely on a fraction of the energy used by a smartphone.\nWhen the station detects rising water risks, it sends lightweight radio signals using LoRa (Long Range) wireless technology. These low-power signals can travel more than a half-mile through city streets and up to five miles in open areas without needing cell towers or power lines. The data arrives instantly at a local central hub, where emergency teams can monitor conditions from miles away.\nMapping flood paths for fast decision making\nAt the central monitoring site, custom server software aggregates data from multiple deployed nodes across a town or watershed. A second, larger AI model analyzes spatial and temporal patterns across the network to generate an interactive web dashboard with predictive maps.\n\u201cThe user doesn\u2019t need to decipher raw data,\u201d Pan said. \u201cThe dashboard assesses risk levels and shows how flooding could spread across monitored locations, highlighting higher-risk zones so local officials can act quickly.\u201d\nThis flood-path visualization supports emergency responders as they make crucial decisions, such as dispatching crews, closing dangerous roads or issuing targeted neighborhood warnings long before floodwaters peak.\nFrom prototype to product\nTo keep the system affordable, Pan used commercially available, low-cost components. The total cost of parts for one prototype sensing station ranges from roughly $150 to $220.\nPan is currently pursuing patent protection for the hardware architecture. The team aims to refine the design into a sleeker, weatherized commercial product suitable for deployment by small coastal municipalities, homeowners\u2019 associations, agricultural operations and industrial sites.\n\u201cOur ultimate goal is to get this technology deployed where it\u2019s needed most,\u201d Pan said. \u201cWhether along the Gulf Coast, across rural Texas counties or in urban story_contract.action: Built a prototype flood station that charges itself from light and runs its AI model on a small chip.
story_contract.change: A flood gauge that needs grid power and a network becomes a self-powered station that judges flood risk on its own chip and signals a hub by radio.
story_contract.affected_people: Emergency responders and residents of street-level flood-prone blocks. No individual is named in any source.
story_contract.consequence: A hub dashboard with predictive maps of how flooding could spread, for emergency responders, per the university.
story_contract.source_limit: Disclosed illustration of the design the university describes. The accuracy is validation accuracy from initial assessments after training, the announcement reports no field result and names no installation.
story_contract.closing_answer: The design says yes. The proof so far is validation accuracy, and no installed place is named.

art_direction.palette_reason: San Antonio under a storm sky: limestone cream and gray carry the street, flood water is muddy brown, galvanized steel gray is kept for the post and housing, warm paper carries the cards, and one amber is kept only for the risk lamp, the flood paths and the half-mile and five-mile tags.
art_direction.shape_language: A straight galvanized post against soft rounded water edges, hand cut limestone curb, lopsided live oak, and small rectangular paper cards with worn corners. The housing is the one boxy machine form with a tilted cap.

lighting.motivation: Low late afternoon storm light from the upper left warms limestone and steel, a cool sky fill from the right shades the post, and every grounded thing casts a long soft shadow to the right.

hero.silhouette: A tall galvanized post with a tilted boxy housing, a small dark solar panel, a whip antenna and a column of four lens marks at four different heights.
hero.finish: Lit upper-left steel edges, cool shaded right side, a rust drip, a dent in the housing cap, a worn panel corner, small lens glints, a chip cutaway with thin traces and a long soft ground shadow.

art_direction.focal_hierarchy: The station and its four marks first, the waterline or risk lamp second, the cards and map third, the street and tree last.
art_direction.motion_language: Water rises at an even speed and marks light as it crosses them, radio rings expand and fade, cards and tags settle without bounce, and the camera holds while objects perform, moving only to follow the water or to pull back.

signature_shot.reason: Water crosses the four marks one at a time and each lights as it is wet, the whole sensing mechanism in one movement.

captions.text: Some people could have ankle-deep water in their yard.
UT San Antonio says the phone warning can come after that.
So its researchers built a flood station.
It charges itself from light and needs no cell tower.
Four optical sensors at different heights watch the water.
A small chip on the station runs the AI itself.
So it judges flood risk without a central server.
Its radio signal can carry more than a half-mile in streets.
In open country, up to five miles, to a hub.
At the hub, a second, larger AI maps flood paths for responders.
The university reports early chip AI validation.
Accuracy was ninety eight point eight two percent.
The announcement reports no field result.
It names no town with an installed station.

files.config/dispatch_rubric.yaml:
# THE BAR LIVES HERE AND NOWHERE ELSE.
#
# Never restate this number in a prompt, a brief, or a verdict file. The sibling lost five panel
# rounds to exactly that: its routine prompt carried one number while this file carried another,
# so the panel was briefed the stale one and returned ship:false on a cut that was already over
# the real bar. Two judges flagged the divergence unprompted and the run kept grading against the
# wrong number anyway.
#
# A number restated in a second place is a number that will be wrong in one of them.
#
# AND THIS HEADER PROVED IT ON 2026-08-19. It used to tell that story by quoting both numbers,
# so the file whose whole job is to hold one bar carried two more in its own comment, four lines
# under the sentence forbidding it. The owner moved the bar that morning and all three judges of
# round 22 reported being briefed the old one; every one of them also flagged that a judge who
# skims this header before reaching the value below reads the stale figure as live. The numerals
# are gone. Anyone who needs the number reads the field.
#
# WHY THE BAR CAME DOWN OFF THE ORIGINAL. The sibling recalibrated with the reason written down:
# the original was implicitly calibrated against a painterly fidelity this brand deliberately
# does not use, so the ceiling on every run became the house style itself, and the panel's
# weakest axis was "the flat vector characters" for nine straight rounds while every concrete
# defect got fixed. A bar that can only be cleared by abandoning the house style is not a bar,
# it is a disagreement about the style, and it belongs in a style decision rather than a score.
rubric:
  # Set by the owner on 2026-08-19, down from where it had been.
  # This is the ONLY place the bar lives and the only place it may be changed.
  # A run does not get to move it: a below-bar final panel remains active repair,
  # and delivery requires the hash-bound passing report. Only verified shipment
  # completes a production run. The owner controls any change to this bar.
  ship_threshold: 7.0

  axes:
    hook:
      weight: 0.18
      asks: >
        Would a stranger stop scrolling in the first two seconds, with the sound off? The first
        frame is the whole decision. A title card is not a hook.
    story:
      weight: 0.20
      asks: >
        Does this feel like Texas AI Docket moving today: a dated actor, decision or application,
        consequence, honest limit, and what happens next? Is there an earned take rather than a
        summary, and does the piece turn somewhere the viewer did not see coming?
    picture:
      weight: 0.20
      asks: >
        Does every five seconds pay in motion, emotion or revelation? Is anything a held slide
        with a voice over it? With captions hidden, does each shot literally depict the sentence
        being spoken rather than reuse generic Texas scenery?
    place:
      weight: 0.14
      asks: >
        Would a Texan from that county believe the person who drew this had been there? Region
        light, vegetation, kit and cast all correct for the story's actual county.
    craft:
      weight: 0.14
      asks: >
        Camera movement motivated by the action; deliberate holds when the subject acts or evidence
        is read. Depth and sound clarify cause and consequence. Type legible at feed size. Nothing
        symmetric that should not be. Maintained but worn, not new and not ruined.
    voice:
      weight: 0.14
      asks: >
        Does the read sound like a person who knows the subject, or like a narrator reading? Are
        captions aligned to the final mix rather than approximated?

  hard_fails:
    # TIGHTENED 2026-08-19, and the wording is the whole of it. This used to read "does not
    # trace to a verified claim", which a judge showed is satisfied by a claim's `statement` or
    # `value_text` -- fields a model writes after reading the source. The film printed a readout
    # row against a claim marked VERIFIED whose fetched quote contained no such figure at all,
    # and every numeral gate stayed green because the numeral was in the authorised set.
    # Measured across that board, five of eleven readout figures sat in no fetched sentence.
    # The evidence is the QUOTE. `super_evidence_check` enforces this over supers and readouts,
    # with a per-claim `quote_is_excerpt` for sources that publish a table, declared rather than
    # inferred. This is a tightening, never a loosening: nothing that passed before on real
    # fetched evidence fails now.
    - a numeral on screen or in the script that does not appear in the fetched QUOTE of a
      verified claim, rather than merely in a statement or value_text written about it; the sole
      exception is a licence-version numeral inside the music.py-generated credit when
      music.py --verify-package binds that exact credit to a verified registry row
    - a caption timing that was approximated, scaled or hand-shifted rather than force-aligned
    - audio time-stretched to fit a cut
    - a region that does not match the story's county
    - a retired motif: six flags, Confederate imagery, lotería, calavera, a headdress
    - a brimmed hat on a rig floor or in a unit
    - a held slide longer than five seconds with no motion, emotion or revelation
    - a narrated idea that is not bound to an actual rendered item and visible change
    - a lead film that falls through to the generic plane renderer with no registered
      cinematic_template, physical throughline, performed turn, bookend and sourced sign-off

  "criteria": {
    "subject_recognition": "The principal subject is immediately recognizable at actual phone size, with enough picture space to understand its action.",

    "dominant_action": "The focal subject performs the narrated transformation. Peripheral motion, an overlay label or camera drift cannot supply missing action.",
    "surface_finish": "Inspect native detail as well as phone size. Surfaces, thickness, joints, light and shadows must look finished for the chosen style.",

    "closing_payoff": "The closing image answers the opening question and makes the source limit understandable without inventing a case outcome.",
    "sound": "Use actual audible-media evidence for voice, masking, sync and motivated sound. Never infer a listening verdict from captions."
  },
  "review_rule": "Ground blocking findings in a timed observed defect and its effect on comprehension or finish. Distinguish uncertainty and optional preferences without weakening mandatory standards. # Finite creative repair and autonomous shipment

Owner instruction from October 3rd, 2026. Read knowledge/craft/AUTONOMOUS_COMPLETION.md before applying older resource-boundary language below. Internal review ceilings and host capacity errors trigger autonomous mandatory completion recovery, never an approval stop or an unfinished-capacity final response. Preserve exact failures, the original frozen envelope and cumulative charges. Only accepted finish --result shipped completes production.

Effective September 29, 2026. The owner requires a shipped video and prohibits stopping for
creative approval. The default limit is three creative repair rounds. Before September 30, each charged
`reboards` unit counts; later editions use the independently classified accounting below. Also stop optional creative
repair earlier after at least one repair and three critic calls when the effective frozen
critic ceiling has fewer than three calls left for another complete correction path. This
protects the final timed-phone review. The controller never resets or silently expands usage.

At that boundary, preserve the strongest reviewed complete cut and finish voice, measured
captions, native hero, final render, every independent audiovisual lens and the three scorers.
Do not start another aesthetic reboard. Correct retained factual or technical failures within
the recorded resources; do not reinterpret them as artistic or declare an incomplete delivery
shipped. Preserve real access/resource failures and continue the executable completion work.

The rubric, score and original pass/revise values remain unchanged. Only motion, surface
finish, pacing polish, ending artistry and style can be deferred. Source accuracy, rights,
readability, comprehension and misleading implications cannot. Native picture occupancy,
current renderer/film hashes, actual audible access, observation coverage, audio measurements,
caption alignment and every delivery gate continue to run. A missing review is never an
artistic defect. Structural motion-floor failures retain their original failed reports; native
proof retains measured failures in `bounded_creative_findings`.

An independent critic can classify an existing exact rejected report in a separate sidecar:

```sh
python scripts/creative_release.py --template --board out/dispatch/storyboard.json --report out/dispatch/phone-critic-current.json --film out/dispatch/openings/b.mp4 --scope phone
python scripts/creative_release.py --board out/dispatch/storyboard.json --report out/dispatch/phone-critic-current.json --scope phone
```

The first command produces a deliberately unapproved template under `creative-assessments`.
Only the original independent reviewer fills its observations and categories after examining
the retained evidence. Bind a preserved film/report path that later retiming cannot overwrite.
Every exact original blocker and failed phone observation must be classified once; unknown or
non-artistic categories refuse release. Retained checks need affirmative observed evidence.
The assessment binds the original report bytes, film, source claims and creative concept.
Keep all original reports untouched. Changes to source, concept or film need current evidence.

New provider/scorer responses include an honest `bounded_release` classification in their
initial immutable response. Obtain all lenses even if the first rejects. The audiovisual tool
adds the classification prompt; scorers read this policy and the same schema helper. A rejected
phone/AV report without concrete defects cannot use a score-only claim. A below-bar panel may
use score-only classification only when it has no separate rejected attention criterion.

`finish --result publishable` records the distinct publication mode and original failures in
controller `bounded_release`; it leaves production active in publishing. The final report card
still carries its genuine score, `ship` value and hard fails. Delivery copies assessments and
their exact rejected evidence. A passing later panel does not conceal earlier artistic
deferrals. `first_panel` success stays false if the panel actually failed.

Completion still requires exact-head CI, merge, deployment, permanent reviewed media bytes,
canonical phone playback through Computer Use, and a correctly addressed unsent Gmail draft
with readback. Only `finish --result shipped` completes production. No approval question or
new paid review is needed merely to classify retained evidence in the existing review scope.

## Accounting and quality correction from September 30, 2026

The three-round cap counts creative corrections. Technical repairs still consume the same
charged reboards, critic calls and frozen resources, but a predeclared technical-integrity
scope does not spend a creative round. The full-path headroom brake still counts all work;
this distinction adds no allowance. Historical editions retain their original accounting.

Before begin-repair, the existing independent critic's exact failure report must include
technical_repair.findings. Each row contains the exact original finding and one category:
source, rights, legibility, layout, technical_audio, captions or runtime. Every original
finding must be covered exactly once, by a reviewer distinct from the director. Motion,
pacing, story and style remain creative. Set repair_scope to technical-integrity in the plan.
Its evidence hash and scope are fixed before edits and checked again at authorization.
Only one reboard per such batch is excluded from creative count; all other charges count.

The finite rule ends optional polish on a credible treatment. It cannot waive a held-slide
structural motion failure or a failed dominant-action observation in new editions.
The known whole-film editorial-v1 screenshot/box treatment and repeated cut directions
are rejected before spending. Use the accepted complete preview as the finishing baseline.
If the initial comparison fails, change the mechanism promptly within the reserved path;
do not spend the remaining budget classifying the same wholesale failure as optional polish.
Keep the original score and rejection when a genuinely limited artistic shortfall is released.
Never ask for creative approval, reset usage, or claim shipment before its real evidence.
